surfaces.part: basin rim ring and water surface (large elliptical opening)
lower tier bowl with water seen from above

answer.evidence: The main body is a round stone basin. The width profile grows from 35 at row 30 to 61 at rows 39-48, then narrows to 55 at row 53. That makes an ellipse of about 23 rows (30-52), with a stone rim ring and teal water with ripples and contents visible inside (evidence b and d). Below it, rows 53-63 form a curved ashlar front rim face of about 11 rows, with stone blocks and dark joints. The central pillar carries two tiered bowls whose water is seen from above, so they also read as ellipses. The star finial and water jets are decor. The column scan at x=31 shows the pillar shaft running down through the basin water.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 14 visible tones per full tile, between the hedge (9) and the well/stall (20/17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so no large flat fills. By eye, the stone rim has several value steps with ashlar blocks shaded one by one. The water has teal ripple rings in multiple tones, the tiered bowls and pillar are shaded separately, and the gold star finial has highlights. Only 8% of dark edge pixels are neutral, and the outlines lean dark teal or blue-grey next to the stone and water, so they read as dark material tones, not a black sticker line. The piece is larger than the references and looks at least as rich as the well and stall, with no flat or thin areas.
